PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-08-29
61M, outpatient visit for a routine check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine outpatient check-up. He reports feeling generally well with steady energy. He follows a reduced-salt diet most days but admits to frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. He works as a bookkeeper, mostly seated, and walks in the evenings. Mother with rheumatoid arthritis. Appetite is good, weight stable, and sleep is adequate. He takes his medications as prescribed and has had no trouble with refills. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 126/78, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 188 lb, BMI 27.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (this week): creatinine 1.5 mg/dL, eGFR 48 mL/min/1.73m2, potassium 4.4 mmol/L, A1c 6.1%, lipid panel within goal.

A/P:
1. Chronic kidney disease stage 3, eGFR 48, stable. Renal function stable on today's labs. Continue to avoid nephrotoxic agents; acetaminophen acceptable for comfort. Repeat renal panel in 6 months.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Family history: reviewed relevant family history with patient and discussed reassurance and routine follow-up.
4. Health maintenance: colorectal screening up to date; influenza vaccine offered this fall. Encouraged balanced meals and hydration.

Return in 6 months to review labs, sooner as needed.
